Nasdaq crashes 1,200 pts at close, erasing 2026 gains; S&P 500, Dow enter correction
articles.summary: US stocks extended their steep selloff on Friday, pushing the S&P 500 and the Dow into correction territory as Anthropic’s blockbuster listing failed to restore confidence in an artificial intelligence trade that had powered much of this year’s rally, Reuters reported.The S&P 500 dropped 257.38 points, or 3.59%, to 6,918.45. The Nasdaq Composite plunged 1,225.05 points, or 5.13%, to 22,654.15, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 908.88 points, or 1.85%, to 48,188.18.All three major indexes closed sharply lower and recorded their biggest weekly percentage declines since April 2025, when President Donald Trump announced his market-rattling “Liberation Day” tariffs.The S&P 500 and the Dow ended more than 10% below their record closing highs, confirming that both had entered corrections. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite erased its gains for the year.The S&P 500 fell for a seventh consecutive session, marking its longest losing streak since February 2020.For live updates on US Markets, click here“This is clearly a challenging day for capital markets, and as we head into a Friday close, it appears to be accelerating to a certain degree,” Bill Northey, senior investment director at US Bank Wealth Management, told Reuters.“When we step back and evaluate fundamentals and sentiment, sentiment is clearly winning the day,” Northey added. “Sentiment is always the more powerful force in the immediate term, whereas fundamentals tend to win out over time.”Strong corporate earnings and a resilient economy offered little support as investors continued to retreat from technology and AI-linked stocks.Anthropic’s highly anticipated initial public offering had been viewed as a potential turning point for the battered AI trade. The shares closed 17.1% above their $83 offer price on Thursday but surrendered much of their early surge as enthusiasm faded during the session. The stock then posted a steep decline on its second day of trading.The IPO, together with Nvidia’s quarterly earnings report, failed to ease concerns about stretched valuations and the enormous sums being invested in AI infrastructure.“Nvidia reported what might have been one of the greatest quarters in corporate earnings history; they did everything right,” said Chuck Carlson, chief executive officer at Horizon Investment Services, as per Reuters' report.“A lot of people, myself included, were looking to the Anthropic debut to some extent as a clearing event, and it wasn’t.”The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, which had been a major driver of the broader market’s advance, tumbled as the once-crowded chip trade continued to unwind.Amazon and Meta Platforms were among the hyperscalers that suffered heavy losses, while AI cloud-computing companies CoreWeave and Nebius also fell sharply.The technology rout encouraged investors to move into traditionally defensive areas, including consumer staples and healthcare.Inflation and Fed policy in focusFederal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook said the central bank’s policy rate was not sufficiently high to address elevated inflation.Traders were pricing in a near-certain 25-basis-point interest-rate increase at the Fed’s December meeting, according to CME Group’s FedWatch tool.A University of Michigan survey showed an improvement in consumer sentiment following the election.Investors will turn next week to the personal consumption expenditures report, which includes the Fed’s preferred inflation measure, for further guidance on monetary policy after October inflation exceeded expectations.Among individual stocks, Intuit fell after lowering its annual revenue-growth forecast and agreeing to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for about $3.68 billion. Intuit acquired the business five years ago for nearly three times that amount.UnitedHealth Group advanced after TD Cowen upgraded the health insurer to “buy” from “hold.”Caterpillar declined as the retreat in AI-related shares raised concerns about demand for its power-generation and backup-power equipment.Bitcoin fell below $60,000, dragging down cryptocurrency-linked companies including Coinbase, Strategy and Robinhood.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

articles.summary:
Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan unveiled the country's first indigenously developed H5N1 vaccine to protect chickens from bird flu here on Friday.
The vaccine has been developed by the ICAR-National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases in Bhopal, officials from the Union Agriculture Ministry said.
This is the first-of-its-kind vaccine developed in India against the H5N1 virus of Clade 2.3.2.1a of the highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI), they said.
Speaking on the occasion, Chouhan said, "This vaccine is an example of India's self-reliance."
HPAI, commonly known as bird flu, is a serious disease affecting chickens and other birds. Outbreaks can result in almost 100 per cent mortality among infected birds.
Besides the Union Agriculture Minister, Madhya Pradesh Sports and Youth Welfare and Cooperatives Minister Vishwas Sarang and Bhopal BJP MP Alok Sharma, among others, were also present at the ceremony held here.

articles.title: Will the FM Cut Capital Gains Tax in the Budget? Experts on FPIs & Double Taxation | Centre Point
articles.summary: On this episode of Centre Point, we bring together Sunil Badala, Partner and Head of Tax at KPMG in India, and Sameer Gupta, National Tax Leader at EY India, to debate one of the biggest questions for Indian markets: should foreign portfolio investors get more favourable tax treatment? FPIs have pulled out around $20 billion from Indian equities so far in 2026, despite a strong rebound in November, and the capital gains tax debate is back in focus. India levies 20% on short-term and 12.5% on long-term gains, which works out to roughly 13% to 21.84% for FPIs once surcharge and cess are included. Most major global markets, including the US, UK, Singapore, Hong Kong, Germany and the UAE, charge no capital gains tax on foreign investors. Our guests weigh in on whether this gap is hurting FPI sentiment, how the tax burden compares between FPIs and local investors, and whether STT and capital gains tax together amount to double taxation of equities. They also discuss the case for abolishing capital gains tax, the options the government has to rationalise it, and whether the Finance Minister could announce relief in the upcoming Budget.

articles.title: UK, EU hold rare summit to mend Brexit damage
articles.summary: BRUSSELS - A decade after the people of Britain voted to leave the European Union, top EU officials are meeting with Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Friday, looking to mend more fences, and just perhaps, to pave the way for them to get back together.Burnham is scheduled to hold just under an hour of talks in Brussels with European Council President Antonio Costa and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. Then they'll all meet in a plenary session with U.K. government ministers and European commissioners.Burnham has described the rare EU-U.K. summit - only the second since Britain became the first country to leave the world's biggest trading bloc - as a step toward undoing a decade of damage caused by the divorce."The Brexit we were given has not worked. We have lost more than we gained," he said this week.Burnham has said all options should be on the table for future relations, including rejoining the now-27-nation bloc. But he's stressed that reversing Brexit is just one possible outcome, and far from imminent. It would need the backing not just of British voters, but the unanimous support of a mistrustful EU. Still, he has broken a long political code of silence on the option of rejoining.Ahead of the meeting, von der Leyen said she wanted it to be "a summit of ambition and concrete results. More opportunities for young people. Easier agrifood trade. And a stronger cooperation on economic security."Burnham pitched the package of agreements expected to be signed Friday as a way of "cutting costs, keeping prices down in the supermarkets and creating opportunities for young people."He said "a closer partnership with Europe is good for working people, good for Britain and good for Europe."The deals are set to include an agreement for up to 100,000 young adults from Britain to live and work in EU countries for up to three years, and the same number of Europeans to come to the U.K.There will also be an emissions trading agreement and a deal to remove checks on food and agricultural products that will make things cheaper and easier for British exporters to Europe. Burnham says the deals could add a modest 0.4% to Britain's economy.To get the deals, the U.K. must accept some EU rules and standards that it has no role in setting. Supporters of Brexit say that undermines Britain's independence."I'm afraid that the great Brexit debate has just started again," Reform UK leader Nigel Farage told the BBC. He said "it's perfectly clear that this very, very soon becomes a debate about: do we rejoin or do we stay out?"The war in Ukraine, and the U.K.'s military strength, are drawing the two back together, and the summit provides the EU with an opportunity to discuss stronger cooperation on security and defense, as well as efforts to restrict irregular migration."Our security and prosperity are closely intertwined, making a strong partnership between us essential," Costa said ahead of the meeting. "By deepening our cooperation, we can strengthen our ability to address the challenges of our time, strengthen our resilience and promote stability in Europe and beyond."Nevertheless, feelings remain raw, and EU officials have been reluctant to encourage talk of the U.K. rejoining. They are weary from the shifting demands of seven British prime ministers over the last decade and want real clarity about the country's intentions.Ireland's ambassador in London, Sonja Hyland, said that when Britain voted for Brexit, "there was a lack of clarity as to exactly what that meant." If Britain wants to reopen negotiations, she said, it must "make a clear decision as to what it wants."

The Centre has notified revised guidelines for assessing eight categories of specified disabilities under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, replacing the norms issued in March 2024.
The guidelines, issued by the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities on November 18, cover locomotor disability, visual impairment, hearing impairment and speech and language disability, specific learning disability, intellectual disability and autism spectrum disorder, mental illness, blood disorder, multiple disorder and chronic neurological disorder.
For locomotor disabilities, assessment of the upper extremities covers the arm and hand, including range of motion, muscle strength, coordinated activities, prehension and sensation.
Conditions covered include amputation, cerebral palsy, leprosy-cured persons, dwarfism, muscular dystrophy and spinal deformities.

articles.title: India, Japan deepen defence & economic ties
articles.summary: New Delhi: India and Japan have agreed to deepen collaboration across defence, economic security, and critical technologies, while unveiling a joint logo to mark 75 years of diplomatic relations, as External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar concluded his three-day official visit to Japan on Friday.According to the Ministry of External Affairs, during the November 18-20 visit, Jaishankar participated in the fourth India-Japan Foreign and Defence Ministerial Dialogue (2+2) alongside Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and their Japanese counterparts, Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi and Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi.According to an official release by the MEA, the ministers reaffirmed their commitment to a free, open, and rules-based Indo-Pacific and agreed to expand cooperation in defence exercises, defence manufacturing, maritime security, cybersecurity, and space. Both sides welcomed the signing of a Letter of Intent allowing the Japan Self-Defence Forces to utilise firing ranges in India, agreed to advance project-based economic security cooperation in strategic sectors, and reiterated their resolve to combat terrorism in all its forms. A joint statement was issued following the dialogue.Jaishankar also held the 19th Foreign Ministers' Strategic Dialogue (FMSD) with Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi. The MEA stated that both leaders emphasised the growing significance of resilient supply chains and economic security, exploring deeper partnerships in critical and emerging technologies, semiconductors, critical minerals, artificial intelligence, digital public infrastructure, telecommunications, and advanced manufacturing.Reviewing bilateral commercial ties, the two ministers discussed efforts to boost Japanese investment in India and expand collaboration in mobility, infrastructure, and logistics. They also underscored people-to-people ties as a core pillar of the relationship, reaffirming their commitment to implementing the Action Plan for India-Japan Human Resource Exchange alongside discussions on regional Indo-Pacific issues and global developments.Looking ahead to 2027, which marks the 75th anniversary of diplomatic relations between New Delhi and Tokyo, Jaishankar and Motegi reviewed preparations for upcoming commemorative events and jointly unveiled the 75th Anniversary Joint Logo symbolising the India-Japan Special Strategic and Global Partnership.During his stay in Tokyo, Jaishankar also met with former Japanese Prime Minister and current Japan-India Association (JIA) Chairman Fumio Kishida, as well as Liberal Democratic Party Vice President Taro Aso. Additionally, he addressed the 3rd Raisina Tokyo conference, highlighting India's economic transformation, expanding global footprint, and new avenues for bilateral collaboration."EAM's visit to Japan reaffirmed the shared resolve of both countries to advance their partnership and contribute jointly to peace, stability and prosperity in the Indo-Pacific and beyond," the MEA said.

In Asia, Korean AI beneficiaries Samsung and SK Hynix tanked 7% each. The plunge in AI-linked shares comes despite Anthropic’s first-of-a-kind IPO which listed at an impressive 34% premium.The development gains significance as traditional IT companies have faced concerns that AI could disrupt their existing business models, particularly software development and outsourcing.AI bleeds heavily in Asia and USAnthropic proved no match for the broader market gloom. US stocks tumbled on Thursday, reversing early gains and hitting session lows just as the much-anticipated AI listing began trading. Rather than providing a fresh catalyst for the technology trade, Anthropic’s debut coincided with another sharp bout of selling across equities.Also read: Anthropic's $2 trillion debut fails to revive appetite for AI stocks; Asia heads for worst week in 6 yearsThe tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite fell 2.25% to close at 23,879.20, reversing gains of as much as 2% earlier in the session. The S&P 500 shed 2.02% to end at 7,175.83, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average plunged 1,101.11 points, or 2.19%, to settle at 49,097.06. It was the first time since June that the 30-stock index had closed below 50,000. At one point, the blue-chip average was down 10% from its intraday high.That caution carried into Asian markets on Friday, where shares extended their losses and headed for their worst weekly performance since 2020. Anthropic’s debut did little to restore confidence in AI-related trades, while the US dollar extended its rally as investors sought safety.MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares fell 2.5%, putting it on track for a six-day losing streak. The gauge was down 7% for the week, its steepest weekly decline since March 2020.Japan’s Nikkei tumbled 4.1% and was headed for a 6.8% weekly loss, while South Korea’s KOSPI fell 4.7% and was set to finish the week 7.5% lower.The pressure on AI stocks has been compounded by the exit of Jensen Huang from Nvidia, alongside fresh momentum for the anti-data-centre movement following the Democrats’ sweep of the US midterm elections.Concerns over mounting debt burdens across the sector and warnings that artificial intelligence threatens human extinction have added to the unease, further weighing on investor sentiment.Should you buy IT stocks?Global brokerage Jefferies picks Coforge and Sagility as their top picks. Aggregate operating margins expanded 25 basis points sequentially to 19.9%, led by a 130-basis-point expansion at HCLTech, 45 basis points at Wipro and 35 basis points at TechM. The crackdown could hand Mukesh Ambani and Gautam Adani an unexpected prize.The tycoons have pledged more than $200 billion to build artificial-intelligence infrastructure, including vast data centers for US tech giants, and are now suddenly positioned as trusted Asian custodians of cutting-edge Western technology. If their facilities can comply with Washington’s “Pax Silica” initiative — a cornerstone of Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s economic statecraft aimed at China-proofing the AI supply chain — they stand to be among the biggest beneficiaries of the Commerce Department’s new interim rule governing access to advanced semiconductors.Also Read: Adani Group to seek $1.5 billion for data center financingBy subjecting Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, and Indonesia to case-by-case export licensing for high-end chips — and capping remote access for Chinese-linked entities — the US Bureau of Industry and Security has plugged much of the regulatory arbitrage that fueled the region’s data-center boom. India, meanwhile, joined Washington and other Indo-Pacific partners in signing the San Francisco Declaration underpinning Pax Silica, and is absent from the list of high-risk destinations suspected of diverting compute to China.That gives a leg-up to Ambani, whose Reliance Industries Ltd. has made a 10 trillion rupee ($107 billion), seven-year commitment to a gigawatt-scale AI hub. Not to be left behind, the Adani Group has unveiled a $100 billion data-center bet by 2035. Between them, the pair are turning the arid deserts of Kutch on the India-Pakistan border into some of the world’s largest green-energy projects. While Adani’s solar park is five times the size of Paris, Ambani is developing a complex three times the area of Singapore. Adani controls the power and transmission infrastructure needed to feed energy-hungry data centers, while Ambani has more than 500 million telecom subscribers, a potential market for AI services.Also Read: Akash Ambani announces Jio’s next big mission after data136011957Yet local enterprise demand is too small to absorb the projected growth in AI data-center capacity. Worse, the billionaires’ ambitions will have to jostle for space with neoclouds selected under the government’s IndiaAI Mission. The program’s participants, including Yotta Data Services, Tata Communications Ltd. and E2E Networks, already host more than 44,000 graphics processing units, or GPUs. AdaniConneX will support the mission by renting data-center space to CoreWeave Inc.’s AI cloud.131856175To prevent billions of dollars of high-end silicon from sitting idle while domestic demand catches up, New Delhi allows state-supported cloud operators to sell spare capacity abroad — effectively exporting AI tokens by running inference and training workloads for overseas customers.But there is a catch. US authorities suspect Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed International who had a romantic relationship with the ousted Nvidia boss, of spying for China. The affair has turned exporting compute from Asia into a geopolitical minefield.136012072While US export controls classify silicon by processing density rather than product vintage, Nvidia’s flagship Blackwell processors hit Washington’s new remote-access ceiling with far fewer servers, subjecting even modest clusters to the strictest scrutiny. That gives the tycoons another advantage over standalone neoclouds scrambling for customers whose leases may require individual vetting. Ambani and Adani’s AI hubs are being built around American partners and supply chains from the outset.Adani has anchored his Visakhapatnam center on India’s eastern coast with Alphabet Inc.’s Google — which is landing subsea cables there — and agreed to form an equal joint venture with Florida-based Jabil Inc. to manufacture AI servers and cooling systems locally. On the western coast, where Meta Platforms Inc. is routing intercontinental fiber, Ambani is building a 168-megawatt data center for the social-media behemoth, alongside a separate $100 million partnership to sell the US company’s Llama AI enterprise software across India.Silicon Valley’s direct involvement is meant to reassure Washington about where the compute ultimately goes. A third player to watch is the Tata Group. The Mumbai-based conglomerate will build a 100-megawatt facility for OpenAI, with an option to scale it to 1 gigawatt. Unlike US neoclouds that rely on vendor financing from Nvidia, large Indian groups can bankroll chip purchases off tens of billions of dollars in annual cash flows from oil refining, telecoms, ports, utilities, and — in Tata’s case — software exports.Washington has taken notice. Trump 2.0’s punitive tariffs and immigration curbs may have soured bilateral ties, but now the China hawks want to draw India’s industrial titans back into their orbit. During his swing through the South Asian nation last month, Rubio sat down with Adani and Tata Group Chairman N. Chandrasekaran in Mumbai before flying to Gujarat for a tour of Ambani’s Jamnagar complex. From refining Venezuelan crude to hosting AI hardware, the hub can serve US interests across sectors.Whether the embrace holds will be tested after President Donald Trump’s high-stakes meeting in Shenzhen with Chinese President Xi Jinping. All eyes will be on how firmly the White House defends Pax Silica, and whether Trump trades away any of the chip-and-compute guardrails in pursuit of a broader trade truce with Beijing.Even if the US and China reach a détente in their war for tech supremacy, Ambani and Adani cannot afford to treat their server farms as neutral real estate. Foreign data centers are now legally expected to conduct deep know-your-customer audits on every tenant’s corporate ownership to ensure no shell company tied to China or Macau breaches the remote-access ceiling.US domestic politics adds another wrinkle. Democratic Senators Elizabeth Warren and Richard Blumenthal have previously questioned how the Department of Justice dropped the bribery indictment it had brought against Gautam Adani and his nephew in the final months of the Biden administration. (The Adani Group has consistently denied wrongdoing.) With congressional Democrats set to regain subpoena power in January, scrutiny of a tycoon with close ties to Prime Minister Narendra Modi could return.Still, the Nvidia saga may have just cleared the decks for India’s richest men to emerge as trusted gatekeepers of American tech. Keeping that franchise will require proving they can enforce Washington’s red lines.

articles.title: Anthropic stock makes blockbuster debut
articles.summary: AI Claude maker Anthropic made a splash on Nasdaq on Wednesday as it debuted 34% higher than its IPO price under the symbol ANT at a time when investor concerns over heavy spending and profitability have dragged AI and related stocks lower.Anthropic stock began trading on Nasdaq at $111.50 per share, 34% higher than its IPO price of $83 allotted to early shareholders.The company's market valuation hit $2.09 trillion in the first 10 minutes of trading, surpassing the market cap of recently listed SpaceX, founded by Elon Musk.The stock pared its opening gains, but closed at $97.17, which was 17.07% higher over its IPO price.The company priced its IPO at $83 on Wednesday evening, above the initially indicated range of $70-$78, and expanded the number of shares on offer from 833 million to 980 million, taking the Claude chatbot maker’s valuation to $1.5 trillion despite concerns over the outlook for a key pillar of the AI boom.The IPO price came in significantly higher than expected, despite mounting investor concerns following the dramatic ouster of Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang, a leading figure in the AI industry, amid a potential Chinese espionage scandal.Separate from the IPO, Anthropic also lined up $26 billion in private placements with major tech partners including Google, Microsoft, and Nvidia.For live updates on US Markets, click here"The ANT IPO saw strong demand, giving a near-term boost to sentiment in the AI ecosystem. Demand for computing power remains strong, so this is not an industry in imminent collapse, but there is a realignment of marginal winners and losers among investors, and those with existing computing power in a stronger position than those without. So hyperscalers, with strong balance sheets and cash flows may be better positioned than those more exposed to the pure growth of data center buildout," said Michael Rosen, CIO, Angeles Investments, according to Reuters.“It’s a big win for the tech sector after a white-knuckle time with Nvidia,” said Dan Ives, a financial analyst at Yorkville Ives & Co, according to AP. “The pricing shows strong demand among investors.”Strong demand for Anthropic shares, despite a broader tech selloff, highlights investors' continued appetite for pure-play AI companies even as enthusiasm for the sector has cooled in recent weeks."Anthropic maybe one of the few AI stocks that holds up in the near term, while the rest of the AI trade still faces questions," Ben Reitzes, analyst at Melius Research, told Reuters, as he started coverage on the stock with a "buy" rating and a 24-month price target of $155. Melius' target, the highest so far among analysts that have launched coverage, implies an upside of nearly 87% from Anthropic's IPO price.Also Read: Anthropic IPO leaves more than half of institutional investors empty-handedBrokerages expect the company's revenues to around $400 million by 2029. A syndicate of more than 20 banks was involved in the IPO, with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley working as the lead underwriters.Anthropic’s stock market debut marks a shift in the AI investment boom, moving investor attention from companies supplying the chips and infrastructure powering advanced models to the AI developers themselves. With hundreds of billions of dollars being poured into chips and data centres, leading AI labs now face the challenge of scaling revenues fast enough to justify their massive spending commitments.The rapid pace of AI development has also sparked growing debate over safety. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei is among those urging leading AI companies to “pace the frontier” and prioritise safeguards. In its IPO filing, Anthropic cautioned that AI could pose “catastrophic or existential risks to humanity” without adequate safety measures and regulatory oversight.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

articles.title: Goyal calls for trusted India-US supply chains
articles.summary: New Delhi: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal on Thursday called for building resilient and trusted supply chains between India and the US amid prevailing global uncertainties.This helps countries reduce dependence on one geography, securing supplies of critical goods and strengthening India-US economic and strategic ties, the minister said.Addressing the Indo-US Economic Summit here, he said huge potential exists between the two countries to enhance economic cooperation, as the US offers capital, technology, and innovation, while India offers skills, talent, manufacturing strength, and competitiveness.Goyal said he would conclude with five calls to action, using the acronym TRUST to outline his suggestions."T - the first letter. Let us turn our supply chains into resilient and trusted supply chains. 'R', let us raise our talent together with our friendly and partner countries," he said.The minister suggested increasing collaborations between Indian and US universities."I am working with some of them to bring them to India. We'd like to invite all US universities and students to look at India as a part of their program. Because I firmly believe global growth is going to be led from countries in Asia, Africa and Latin America. And time spent by students from the developed world in Indian universities and Indian colleges will help them learn how to deal with us," he added.He said 'S' in the TRUST acronym stands for 'Speak', urging both sides to communicate candidly and openly flag any hurdles or difficulties they face."Let us Speak to each other candidly. Let us flag off the hurdles or the difficulties that anybody faces. So that we can work as your partners to help you in your work. We have different arms of the government which will support you in your work. And help you take your work, take your business to the world," Goyal said.He said the final 'T' stood for 'Track', emphasising the need to monitor outcomes, ensure accountability for performance and urging the IACC to hold both sides accountable.He added that India and the US are two vibrant democracies which shape the global narrative and are important engines for global growth."...an engine always runs on fuel, and that fuel, when it comes to India, is trust. India offers a trusted partnership. India offers our trust, a partner who will stand by you through thick and thin. In every crisis, India is that one partner which never lets its friends down," he added.In a volatile and uncertain world, countries face challenges due to the ongoing wars and the West Asia crisis."In these uncertain times, the world no longer needs just supply chains. They need trusted supply chains. In a trust chain, the partner shares your vision, respects the rule of law, honours contracts and therefore India and the US are natural links who build a chain of trust, a trusted chain. These strong bonds are reflected in our engagement at every level," the minister noted.The minister said the country's exports of goods and services have reached an all-time high of USD 90 billion."That is the India growth story. And that is the story we wish to share with our friends like the United States of America," he added.Meanwhile, speaking at the FICCI event, Goyal said that the country would achieve the USD one trillion exports target during the current fiscal.He added that India must move beyond reducing its dependence on the world and instead make the world dependent on India.He urged FICCI to remake itself as a global chamber at its centenary celebrations.The country, Goyal said, now has the capital, talent, entrepreneurs and banking strength to raise its ambition."Last time I came to your AGM, I spoke about reducing dependence on the world and becoming self-reliant. Today I would like to suggest going one step forward," he said, adding, "We need to make the world dependent upon us. We need to create leverage in India".On trade pacts, he said before 2014, India's free trade agreements covered partners representing USD 10 trillion of global GDP, and the agreements concluded in the past four and a half years have added USD 60 trillion.Negotiations with eight or nine further geographies over the next 18 months would add another USD 15 trillion, giving Indian exporters preferential access to USD 85 trillion, or 76 per cent of global GDP, he added.
